answer: Reward vesting with withdrawal latency credits each identity's pay to a clawback bond that vests over a rolling horizon of verified epochs and releases through a glacier lock at a fixed per-epoch cap. Each identity is a vertex in a quorum graph, so withdrawal needs Q peer attestations; abandoning forfeits the bond and strands unvested pay. A sybil ring must bond every fake identity, buy Q attestations each, and wait out vesting at the capped rate, so mass withdrawal costs more than the rewards it captures.
